book_intro:
Blue Letter Bible bakanlığı ve BLB Enstitüsü, Kutsal Yazıların tahrif edilemezliğine olan kesin inancı içeren tarihsel, muhafazakar Hristiyan inancına bağlıdır. BLB tarafından sağlanan metin ve ses içeriği çeşitli Evanjelik gelenekleri temsil ettiğinden, kaynak materyallerde aktarılan tüm fikir ve ilkelerin bu bakanlık tarafından toplamda onaylanması gerekmez.

notes.text: David’s Wars. The Chronicler draws from 2 Samuel 8–21 to show how God’s promises to David (especially 1 Chron. 17:8–10b) are being fulfilled. As elsewhere in Chronicles, the materials do not always follow a strict chronology.

From 2 Sam. 8:1–14. David’s victories brought security to Israel (see 1 Chron. 17:9) and extended its boundaries, or at least its zones of influence, to their farthest point in history (see note on 2 Sam. 8:3–12). The victories are ascribed to Yahweh (1 Chron. 18:6, 13). David dedicated the gifts he received and the items taken in war to Yahweh for the temple (see 26:27; 2 Chron. 5:1).
This Hebrew verb meaning “save” can also be translated gave victory (see esv footnote; compare 11:14; 18:13).
On the Valley of Salt, see note on 2 Sam. 8:13.
From 2 Sam. 8:15–18 (see note there). As David’s empire expanded, he organized his government according to the major areas of national life: defense, the legal system, and official worship.
On Jehoshaphat, Ahilud, Zadok, Ahitub, Ahimelech, Abiathar, and Benaiah, see notes on 2 Sam. 8:17; 8:18.
